short: Sweden's soldier king, at war continuously from the age of seventeen until his death.
full:
Charles XII was fourteen when he succeeded his father in April 1697, and the Estates declared him of age at once rather than appoint a regency. In 1700 Denmark, Saxony-Poland and Russia attacked the empire together, expecting to divide it. He forced Denmark out of the war within months, destroyed a much larger Russian army at Narva in November, and then spent six years in Poland removing Augustus the Strong from its throne.

He was personally austere - no wine, no mistress, a plain blue coat - and lived in the field on the same terms as his soldiers, which explains much of the Carolean army's willingness to follow him. He was also unwilling to treat from anything short of victory, and turned down peace offers after Narva and again after Poltava. He spent five years in Ottoman exile following that defeat, returned to Swedish territory in 1714, and was shot at Fredriksten in 1718. Sabaton's "Carolus Rex" and "The Carolean's Prayer" are both about him and his army.
